w: It was a festive day today because the day marked the occasion when Shriji Maharaj initiated Gunatitanand Swami as a sadhu in Dabhan and announced that he was Aksharbrahm - His divine abode. To highlight this festive day, a few youths had prepared a decorative path of flowers for Swamishri. All night long they had devoutedly arranged flowers and petals from Swamishri's residence to the mandir steps. And before the murtis in the mandir, a diksha ceremony atmosphere had been created. Shriji Maharaj was dressed in white clothes and the murtis of Gunatitanand Swami and Gopalanand Swami were donned in saffron clothes. A small pit with a fire burning in it had been arranged before Thakorji. After Swamishri performed the arti, the sadhus sang Vedic mantras in conjunction with the diksha initiation arrangement. Swamishri offered grains and ghee into the fire pit and then applied a chandlo of sandle~wood paste on the murtis. The atmosphere became charged with divinity. It seemed as if a yagna had been really performed and a diksha ceremony had just taken place.

In the evening an assembly, paying tribute to the 190th Diksha ceremony occasion of Gunatitanand Swami took place. In his blessings, Swamishri said, "Shriji Maharaj revealed the glory of Gunatitanand Swami during his diksha ceremony saying that Mulji Sharma was His divine abode. We too have also to take this Akshar-diksha. Akshar-diksha means to understand the form and glory of Akshar and then understand the glory of Purushottam. Once you have understood this, nothing more need be understood.... Shastriji and Yogiji Maharaj had spread this knowledge of Akshar and Purushottam. If one understands this then one's soul will forever become happy."
After lunch Swamishri blessed a group of 15 deaf-dumb youngsters from Bhavnagar who had come to Amdavad to see the Sastha's publishing house - Swaminarayan Aksharpith.

In the Kishore Day assembly, a traditional dance was performed by kishores. Thereafter, kishores who have remained steadfast in niyams were introduced. Then a drama 'Patelnu Hatanu' explaining the need to prioritize moksha in one's life was performed. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly.

A special morning assembly was held to celebrate ‘Rural Day’ in which devotees from the surrounding villages had gathered. The assembly agenda included discourses, a drama ‘The Glory of That Soil’, a dance on “Ham hai Bharat ke Juvan” and Swamishri’s blessings.

After his angiography Swamishri was asked, “Were you under tension?” Swamishri replied with great ease, “I was engaged in bhajan and darshan of Harikrishna Maharaj.” Then Swamishri revealed, “While the angiography was going on, I was engaged in Harikrishna Maharaj’s darshan. Then I distinctly recalled the occasion when Shastriji Maharaj gave me diksha as a sadhu. At night Harijivandas (Swami) talked to me (about taking the sadhu diksha). After I consented, Shastriji Maharaj embraced me and instructed me to tell Yogi Bapa to perform the (next day’s) mahapuja later (than normal) in the morning. When (Swami) was giving me diksha in (Akshar Deri) Yogi Bapa was before me. Shastriji Maharaj told Yogi Bapa to bless me so that I would receive virtues like him. I recollected everything. I offered prostrations to him. I remembered all this clearly, and was also chanting the name of Swaminarayan. My eyes were closed, and when I opened them I would have darshan of the murti of Harikrishna Maharaj.” During the tense medical investigation Swamishri was unworried and absorbed in God and the memories of his guru.
After his angiography, as experiences in the cath lab were being talked about, an attendant sadhu asked Swamishri, "Did you feel any tension during the angiography?"

Swamishri said, "Tension about what? I was doing bhajan, and in front of me was the murti of Harikrishna Maharaj, and I was doing his darshan." Then, sharing something deeper, Swamishri said, "On one side the angiography was going on. Doing darshan of Harikrishna Maharaj in front of me, I fell into thought, and the whole moment when Shastriji Maharaj made me a sadhu came back to me exactly. At night Harjivandas told me, and Shastriji Maharaj embraced me in the middle of the night. In the morning he told Yogi Bapa to hold the mahapuja late. During the diksha, Jogi Bapa sat in front. Shastriji Maharaj was sitting, and the diksha ceremony was taking place at the Akshar Deri. When Shastriji Maharaj gave me the sadhu diksha, he said to Jogi Bapa, 'Bless him so that he gets qualities like yours.' All of that came back to me. I did dandvat to them. All of this came back exactly."

ds.t: Saving money matters more than spending it
w: Ajmera's son had flown from Mumbai to Delhi to do seva at Delhi Akshardham. His grandfather had taught him that, in keeping with the family's standing, he should always travel first class. But he travelled economy class and saved 7,500 rupees. He came to offer this amount to Thakorji in Swamishri's presence.
Swamishri was pleased with his feeling and said, "Saving money is more important than spending it."
In this way, taking an interest in a young boy, Swamishri taught him practical wisdom.

After darshan of Thakorji, Swamishri came down by the hydraulic lift. Students from the hostel were sitting here. When Swamishri came near, one of them said, "This one says that the one coming is Shriji Maharaj, and this other one says it is Pramukh Swami. Who are you?"
Swamishri said, "I am a sadhu, a servant of Shriji Maharaj."

The evening satsang assembly celebrated Swamishri’s 72nd diksha anniversary. It was themed upon the virtues of a true sadhu highlighted in the Ramayan, Bhagavad Gita and the Shrimad Bhagvat. The entire programme was interspersed with video shows, speeches by sadhus and a cultural dance by BAPS children and youths. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the assembly describing how Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj had endeavoured in establishing mandirs and satsang. They served with humility, tolerance and faith in Bhagwan Swaminarayan. “Yogiji Maharaj served in the kitchen. In Gondal, while the mandir construction work was going on, he would wake up at 4.00 a.m. Our tradition is one of humility and service. The 500 paramhansas abided by the moral disciplines prescribed for sadhus and remained focussed on pleasing Maharaj.”
